question: A 72-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of blurry vision for the past 3 days. He has also had 4 episodes of right-sided headaches over the past month. He has no significant past medical history. His father died of coronary artery disease at the age of 62 years. His temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), pulse is 94/min, and blood pressure is 232/128 mm Hg. Fundoscopy shows right-sided optic disc blurring and retinal hemorrhages. A medication is given immediately. Five minutes later, his pulse is 75/min and blood pressure is 190/105 mm Hg. Which of the following drugs was most likely administered?

enhanced_information: The 72-year-old man presents with blurry vision, headaches, and severely elevated blood pressure (232/128 mm Hg), indicating a possible hypertensive emergency with risk of end-organ damage, as evidenced by optic disc blurring and retinal hemorrhages. Immediate treatment is required to lower blood pressure rapidly. Labetalol and Nitroprusside are both effective for acute blood pressure control. Labetalol is commonly used in hypertensive emergencies due to its rapid action and ability to lower both blood pressure and heart rate, as seen with the pulse decrease to 75/min and blood pressure reduction to 190/105 mm Hg. Nitroprusside is also effective but is typically reserved for more severe cases or when immediate control is critical. Hydralazine, while effective, is slower acting and less preferred for immediate management. Nicardipine and Fenoldopam are less commonly used in acute settings. Given the rapid response in this case, Labetalol is the most likely medication administered.
analysis: The patient presents with symptoms indicative of a hypertensive emergency, including severely elevated blood pressure, blurry vision, and signs of end-organ damage (optic disc blurring and retinal hemorrhages). In such cases, rapid blood pressure control is crucial to prevent further complications. Labetalol is a commonly used medication in hypertensive emergencies due to its ability to quickly lower blood pressure and heart rate, as evidenced by the patient's pulse decrease and significant blood pressure reduction after administration. Nitroprusside is also effective but is typically reserved for more severe cases or when immediate control is critical. Given the rapid response observed in this patient, Labetalol is the most likely medication administered. Other options like Hydralazine, Nicardipine, and Fenoldopam are less preferred for immediate management in this context. Therefore, the best-supported option is Labetalol.
